section.title: Introduction
section.p: OmniDisc puts an icon on the icon bar for each drive of the filing systems it has been told about, and gives each a menu of the operations that can be performed on that drive. It works with the filing systems that are based on FileCore (ADFS, SCSIFS, SDFS, RAMFS and similar), and it is started with the desktop as one of its filers. Directories are displayed by the Filer: OmniDisc asks it to open them.

OmniDisc does not format, verify or check discs itself. It starts the programs which have been set up for those operations, and passes them the details of the drive. Showing the contents of a directory, copying files and saving them belong to the Filer and the applications that save to the drive.

section.title: Overview
section.p: OmniDisc is a module which runs as a desktop task. The user, or the system's boot sequence, tells it which filing systems to show with , and may choose the sprites its icons use with . The task is then started as part of the desktop with *Desktop; it is not started by running directly. Drives which are shown by OmniDisc should not also be shown by another filer.

For each drive that exists on a registered filing system there is one icon, showing the sprite chosen for that drive and, below it, the name of the disc in it. Clicking on the icon opens the disc's root directory in the Filer, and the Menu button opens a menu of the operations that can be performed. Files dragged to the icon are opened in the root directory of the disc, and applications saving to the icon are given a filename in it.

subsection.title: Starting and stopping
subsection.p: OmniDisc is started with the desktop's other filers. It answers by giving the command %Desktop_OmniDisc and claiming the call, which makes the desktop start the OmniDisc task. OmniDisc uses the Filer to display the contents of a drive, so the Filer must also be running.

The task registers itself with the Wimp as OmniDisc, as a Wimp 3.10 task, and quits when it receives a Quit message. When the Filer is about to die, OmniDisc tells its task to quit; after a reset it forgets that it has a task.

subsection.title: Filing systems and drives
subsection.p: A filing system is registered with OmniDisc by name. Only a filing system that is built on FileCore and has a disc operations SWI can be registered: OmniDisc looks for <name>_DiscOp, and if there is no such SWI tries the name with FS added or taken off (so SCSI finds SCSIFS_DiscOp). The names RAM and RAMFS both find the SWIs of RamFS. It also uses the filing system's _Drives, _MiscOp and _DescribeDisc SWIs if it has them.

A filing system can have up to eight drives, numbered 0 to 7. Drives 0 to 3 are treated as floppy discs, and the others as hard discs. When a filing system is registered OmniDisc finds the drives it has, and afterwards keeps up to date with them as the filing system reports drives being added and removed with the upcalls and .

The name shown under a drive's icon is the name of the disc in it, as the filing system describes it. For a floppy disc drive the name is shown only if the filing system was registered with -fdnames, as reading it requires the disc to be accessed; otherwise, and for any drive whose disc has no name, the icon is labelled :n, where n is the drive number.

subsection.title: Icon sprites
subsection.p: The sprite for a drive's icon is chosen from the icons set with . Each such icon says which filing system, which disc and which drives it applies to, and may leave any of these out, to apply to any. For a drive, every icon which applies is given a score, and the highest score is used; when two have the same score the one which was added first is used. The score is the sum of

value-table.value: a filing system (all icons score 1 more than this, so an icon which names nothing scores 1)
a disc with this name, compared without regard to case

subsection.p: An icon which names a filing system, a disc or drives that this drive does not match does not apply to it at all. A more specific icon therefore always wins over a less specific one: an icon for a particular disc on a filing system beats one for all the drives of that filing system.
If no icon applies, the sprite is a default, chosen by the filing system and whether it is one of the floppy drives (0 to 3):

value-table.value: floppy drives: floppydisc; other drives: harddisc

subsection.p: The sprites are taken from the Wimp sprite pool.

subsection.title: Order of the icons on the icon bar
subsection.p: The icons are placed on the icon bar by priority, so drives of the same kind are grouped together. OmniDisc uses the priorities of the icon bar specification:

value-table.value: Volatile filing systems, such as RAMFS

subsection.p: The priority of a drive is that for volatile filing systems for RAMFS, for network filing systems for Net and ShareFS, for CD-ROM for CDFS, and for accelerators for ResourceFS. For any other filing system it is that of floppy discs if the drive is removable, and that of hard discs if it is not. Icons are created in the order in which the filing systems are registered, and are placed according to that within a priority.

subsection.title: Using the icons
subsection.p: Clicking Select on a drive's icon opens its root directory in the Filer, as %Filer_OpenDir fs::disc.$, using the drive number if the disc has no name.
Clicking Menu on a drive's icon opens a menu, titled with the drive (ADFS::4), which has these entries. Choosing an entry with Adjust leaves the menu open.

subsection.title: Saving and dropping files on an icon
subsection.p: When an application saves a file by dragging its icon to a drive's icon, the application sends a to OmniDisc. OmniDisc replies with , giving the leaf name as a path in the root directory of the disc (fs::disc.$.leafname), so the file is saved there.

When files are dragged from the Filer to the icon, OmniDisc is sent . It replies with , giving the root directory of the disc as the path to which the Filer should open the files, and then asks the Filer to open that directory with . A which did not come from the Filer is acknowledged with , and the directory is opened.

subsection.title: External tools
subsection.p: The Format, Verify and Check entries of the menu start programs which are set up for the purpose. For each of these OmniDisc looks for an alias, for the kind of disc (Floppy for drives 0 to 3 and Hard for the others) and the filing system, and if it is not set, one for the kind of disc alone. For Format of a floppy disc on ADFS it looks for Alias$@FSFormat_Floppy_ADFS and then Alias$@FSFormat_Floppy. The menu entry does nothing if neither is set. See and .

sysvar-definition.name: Alias$@FS*_*_*
sysvar-definition.description: Program to run for a disc operation on a filing system

use.p: The name is Alias$@FS, then the operation (Format, Verify or Check), an underscore, the kind of disc (Floppy or Hard), an underscore, and the name of the filing system, as it was registered with . For example, Alias$@FSVerify_Hard_SCSIFS.

Its value is the command, or the program, which OmniDisc starts for that operation on drives of that kind of the filing system. It is given the arguments described in External tools. It is used in preference to .

sysvar-definition.name: Alias$@FS*_*
sysvar-definition.description: Program to run for a disc operation on any filing system

use.p: The name is Alias$@FS, then the operation (Format, Verify or Check), an underscore, and the kind of disc (Floppy or Hard). Its value is the command which OmniDisc starts for that operation on drives of that kind, when there is no variable for the filing system.

section.title: Error messages
section.p: The module allocates the errors from &hex;821A00.

use.p: There was not enough memory to add the filing system or icon, or to read a command.

The filing system given to with -add is already registered.
The filing system given to with -add is not one OmniDisc can show: it has no disc operations SWI, so it is not built on FileCore, or it is not running.
There is no icon with the filing system, disc and drives given to with -update or -remove.
An icon has already been set for the filing system, disc and drives given to with -add.
An error which the module does not describe.

This command starts the OmniDisc task in the desktop. It is the command which the module gives the desktop to run in place of the Filer's icon bar, and it is not meant to be used directly: use *Desktop to start the desktop.

command-definition.name: OmniDisc_FS
command-definition.description: Add or remove a filing system, or list those registered
command-definition.parameter: The name of the filing system to add to OmniDisc.
Show the names of the discs in the floppy disc drives (0 to 3) under their icons, rather than the drive number.
The name of the filing system to remove from OmniDisc. Its icons go, and so do the icons which were set for it.
List the filing systems which are registered, with the number of each and its drives that have discs in them.

use.p: This command registers a filing system, so that OmniDisc shows an icon for each of its drives, removes one, or lists them. The filing system has to be one that OmniDisc can show, as described in Filing systems and drives. The icons appear on the icon bar in the order that the filing systems are registered in.
The list gives the name of each filing system, its number, and then for each drive that has a disc, the number of the drive and the name of the disc (nothing if it has no name).

command-definition.name: OmniDisc_Icon
command-definition.description: Choose the sprite used for a filing system, disc or drives, or list the choices
command-definition.parameter: The name of a sprite in the Wimp sprite pool, to use for the icon. It has to exist when the icon is added.
The name of the sprite to change the icon to.
Remove the icon with the filing system, disc and drives given.
List the icons which have been set.
The filing system the icon is for, which has to be registered. If it is not given the icon is for any filing system.
The name of the disc the icon is for, which is compared without regard to case. If it is not given the icon is for any disc.
The drives the icon is for, as a string of the digits of the drive numbers, such as 45 for drives 4 and 5, or 0123 for all the floppy drives. If it is not given the icon is for any drive.

use.p: This command sets the sprite which is used for the icons of drives, or lists those set. An icon applies to the drives which match the filing system, disc and drives that were given when it was set, and any of them may be left out to match any. When more than one icon applies to a drive the most specific is used, as described in Icon sprites. A drive that no icon applies to gets the default sprite for its filing system.

To update or remove an icon, the filing system, disc and drives must be given exactly as they were when it was added. The error is returned if there is no such icon, and if an icon is added which is already set.
The list shows the sprite, the filing system, the disc and the drives of each icon, with <ANY> where it was left out.
